label: paragraph_title
text: TO TREAD WARILY.

label: text
text: BRITAIN AND CHINA.

label: text
text: WELL-INFORMED CORRESPONDENT'S OPINION.

label: text
text: That failing action on the part of the Chinese themselves to re-store conditions under which trade will be possible, business men in China have little to hope in the matter of an early settlement from the policy of the British Government, is to be read between the lines of an article by the always well informed political correspondent of the “Manchester Guardian Weekly,” in the August 26 issue. It would be optimistic to predict that much less than a twelve month will have to elapse before a final settlement could be reached on the lines of the elaborate machinery he outlines as that which in the considered opinion of the Government is necessary for the problem to be dealt with satisfactorily.

label: text
text: He writes as follows:—

label: text
text: The Canton Government's embargo on shipping and the rest of the troubles in China, in the absence of any central Government whose writ runs through China, is a very serious problem for the Foreign Secretary and the Foreign Office.

label: text
text: The Canton Government is the Government of the National People's party, a more or less "Red" party, but especially the heir of the late Sun Yat-sen's policy. The British Government is engaged at present in examining the treaties which regulate our relations with China and with Chinese ports. It is their opinion at present that the action of the Canton Government is a breach of these treaties, which provide for the completest freedom for British traders, a freedom which is obviously violated by the regulations now issued by the Canton Government.

label: text
text: The whole of the troubles in China are part of one problem, which is, in effect, the break-up of the central control of the Chinese Empire as directed from Peking. The British Government has not been inactive, but in view of the internal situation in China and the international situation outside China it must tread very warily. So far, its line of approach to the problem is as follows:

label: text
text: THE IMMEDIATE PROBLEMS.

label: text
text: First, with regard to Shanghai we are about to hold a public judicial inquiry into the riots. This is not an attempt to whitewash anybody, but is designed to bring all the facts out and ensure that justice shall be done. We have tried to get the Chinese Government to appoint representatives, but, much to our regret, the Chinese Government has refused.

label: text
text: Thirdly, the British Government seeks to arrange a collective answer by all the Powers to the various Chinese Notes that have been presented, and particularly to the Note of July 24, in which the Chinese complained of the unfairness of the various treaties. Our wish is that this Note should be a declaration of policy by all the Powers. The first thing is to carry out the conclusions of the Washington Conference, and the first step is the Tariff Conference, which is now very soon to be held. At the same time there follows the setting up of a commission to inquire into the whole subject of extraterritoriality.

label: text
text: Secondly, negotiations have been begun between the diplomatic bodies at Peking and the Chinese Government on subjects connected with Shanghai though not in connection with the actual riots. One of the subjects so discussed is the representation of the Chinese on the Municipal Council of Shanghai. At present the rate-payers elect the Council, which in practice means the Europeans. The Council consists of Europeans, Americans, and Japanese, and its present chairman is an American.

label: text
text:
The collective answer of the Powers to the Chinese Notes is still under consideration. It will be a slow business, because a complete consultation involves sixteen Powers with a right to be consulted. The British Government lays the great stress upon this collective action, and has the greatest interest in any action being collective, because there is an attempt in China, largely due, as the Foreign Office believes, to Russian Influence, to isolate Great Britain and represent her as the villain of the piece.

METHODIST ACTIVITY IN YUNNAN

label: text
text: NEW BUILDING OPENED:

label: text
text: (From Our Own Correspondent.)

label: text
text: Yunnanfu, Sept. 8.

label: text
text: On Friday, September 4; in glorious weather, the new Methodist Church building was opened in the presence of a large gathering.

label: text
text: The new building, which accommodates about 300 people, is about 100 feet by 40 feet, and is constructed on principles new to this city.

label: text
text: There are no pillars, the structure of the roof being of steel on the cantilever principle, the material for which was shipped out from England. These slender rods stretching across and upwards look very spidery, but the strength is there, and more than sufficient.

label: text
text: Representatives of all the Churches were seated on the rostrum, and each spoke a few words of encouragement and hope for the future of the church in Yunnanfu.

label: text
text:
The Rev. A. Evans, who super-intended the entire work from beginning to end, is in charge of the work of the Methodist Church in Yunnanfu, and great credit is due to him for the splendid building resulting from his efforts.
The building was well-filled at this opening ceremony, and all the foreign missionaries were present.

label: text
text: At each side of the Church are several class-rooms shut off by folding doors from the main building, but which may be used for accommodating another 200 people if necessary. The acoustics of the building leave nothing to be desired.

label: text
text: After the opening ceremony, the visiting members—both Chinese and foreign—sat down to a Chinese feast in an adjoining building, and all thoroughly enjoyed it.

label: text
text: A collection towards the expenses of the new church was taken up during the proceedings, and $127.00 was realised.

label: text
text: Whatever else the church stands for, it certainly stands for Faith, as it is hoped to be filled with church members in the future.

label: text
text: On the Sunday following the opening, the building was taxed to its utmost capacity by the numbers present, and as there was a good deal of coming and going, it is probable that almost 1,000 people were present at some time or other on Sunday only.

label: text
text: At such a time as this, it seems a bold thing to build a new church in any part of China, but only the future can show the justification for it.

label: paragraph_title
text: COAL THEFT.

label: paragraph_title
text: LAUNCH MEN IN TROUBLE.

label: text
text: IMPORTANT KOWLOON CASE

label: text
text: Fraudulent conversion of five tons of coal entrusted to their care, with the alternative charge of larceny of the coal, was preferred against three men from the Blue Funnel launch "Poseidon" at the Kowloon Magistracy yesterday. Two other members of Messrs. A. S. Watson's launch "Tai Yuk Fong" were charged with receiving the coal knowing the same to have been stolen or unlawfully obtained.

label: text
text: Mr. D. McCallum, appearing for the three Blue Funnel launch men, objected to two charges being preferred against his clients in alternative forms, but this was not upheld.

label: text
text: Mr. J. M. d'Almada Renedios defended the alleged receivers.

label: text
text: Mr. T. G. Bennett, who prosecuted on behalf of the complainants, the Ocean Steamship Company, asked for a committed to the Sessions.

label: text
text: The story for the prosecution was that the transfer of coal was noticed to be going on from the "Posidon" to the "Tai Yuk Fong." The superintendent of Holt's wharf was informed and on an inspection being made it was discovered that about five tons of coal had been transferred from the Blue Funnel launch. The boatswain was paid $860 per month to purchase coal and pay the wages of the crew of the "Tai Yuk Fong," while the requirements of the "Posidon" were attended to by the Company.

label: text
text: After evidence had been called the case was adjourned till this afternoon.

label: paragraph_title
text: MOROCCO FIGHTING.

label: text
text:
FURTHER OFFENSIVE
IMMINENT

label: text
text: FRENCH STRATEGY.

label: text
text: (Router's Service.)

label: paragraph_title
text: Paris, Sept. 21.

label: text
text: The "Echo de Paris" war correspondent at Morocco states that 80 battalions are shortly to participate in a big new French offensive on the Kiffane sector, north of Taza, the success of which will result in the submission of some wavering tribes and will considerably reduce the enemy zone, separating Kiffane from the Spanish post at Azibdemidor in the Melilla sector.

label: text
text: A communiqué from Madrid reports the enemy's gunfire on the Alhucemas sector has intensified, but everything is quiet on the Ceuta and Tetuan sector.

label: paragraph_title
text: NEW PLAN SUCCESSFUL.

label: text
text: The new plan of reprovisioning has successfully been tested, dispensing with mules and substituting carts drawn by tanks and con-voyed by infantry, while the planks are protected by artillery barrage.

label: text
text: Paris newspapers learn from Madrid that a Spanish offensive is imminent, the object being to capture Abd el Krim's headquarters at Ajdir. General Primo de Rivera is reported to have placed cavalry detachments at the disposal of Marshal Petain.

label: text
text: TO CONFER.

label: text
text: General Primo di Rivera has arrived at Alhucemas to confer with General San Jurjo with regard to forthcoming operations.

label: paragraph_title
text: PARIS CUT OFF.

label: text
text: STRIKE OF TELEGRAPH OPERATORS.

label: text
text: "A LAST WARNING:"

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Paris, Sept. 21.

label: text
text: A strike of telegraph and telephone operators cut off Paris from the outside world for two hours this morning.

label: paragraph_title
text: TWO HOURS ONLY.

label: text
text: The strike was organised for only two hours as “a last warning to the authorities.”

label: text
text: There was no demonstration, but the strikers remained in the Central Telegraph office and listened to speeches of leaders.

label: text
text: A delegation waited on the Minister of Posts to protest against the alleged discrimination in the matter of wages against them.

label: paragraph_title

EMBARGO RAISED.

label: text
text: LANCASHIRE PLEASED.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: London, Sept. 21

label: text
text: Lancashire textile concerns are pleasantly surprised at the announcement of the news of the removal of all restrictions on the import of textiles to Germany.

label: text
text: The Manchester Chamber of Commerce last year complained to the then Premier, Mr. Ramsay MacDonald, of the German import licence system which practically excluded British textiles, and urged a modification in the Anglo-German Trade Treaty, then being negotiated.

label: text
text: Germany promised consideration of the complaint and has now ratified a clause of the treaty completely raising the embargo.

label: paragraph_title
text: LESS TEA:

label: text
text: It is reported "sterling" ten companies, through the India Tea Association in London have decided to restrict the output of tea from North India to the figure for 1924.

label: text
text: The Indian Tea Association of Calcutta is also said to have decided to adopt a similar restriction of "rupoo" companies.

label: text
text: London, September 21

label: text
text:
Art collectors are surprised at the announcement of the cancellation of the forthcoming sale of the extensive collection of works of art contained in the late Lord Leverhulme's house at Hampstead.
The auctioneers state that an offer has been received from the Anderson Galleries, New York, which it is impossible for them to advise Lord Leverhulme's executors to refuse, though the executors have the right to reserve any of the contents which it may be desired to purchase one behalf of the nation.

label: text
text: The Anderson Galleries will hold a sale on behalf of the executors in New York next year.

label: paragraph_title
text: LINER SAILS FROM CAPE TOWN.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text:
Cape Town, September 21.
The Arundel Castle sailed for England with 130 passengers, carrying 120 firemen and trimmers recruited locally, many of them Dutch-speaking South Africans.

label: text
text: London, September 21. Mr. F. C. Allen, chairman of the Shipping Federation, in a long statement declares that "the so-called weamens' strike is really a reconnaissance in force in connection with" the general communist offensive by direct action against the existing order of society." He emphasises that no protest against the agreement for the wages reduction of July 3, was made until August 12 and asserts that the leaders of the agitation are nearly all avowed communists and very few are seamen. Their principal weapon is terrorism. He exhorts the Governments of Britain and the Dominions to take measures to enable the men to carry out their lawful avocations under agreed conditions.

label: text
text:
Cape Town, September 21.
It is understood that the Cabinet has decided to suggest to the Imperial Government to appoint a board of enquiry in England to investigate the functioning of the muritium board, and other matters connected with the scamens strike, as it had reason to believe in the suggestion finding favour with both sides, and if adopted would probably result in calling off the strike. Mr. Hertzog informed Mr. Creswell that he is willing to receive a deputation of the strikers.

label: paragraph_title
text: OBFITUARY

label: text
text: New York, Sept. 21.

label: text
text: Mr. Alfred Bedford, Chairman of the Standard Oil Company of New York has died at New Jersey.

label: text
text: Chairman of the parent body before the dissolution some ten or fifteen years ago and chairman at the present day of the Board of Directors of the largest of the Standard Oil branches, Mr. A. Bedford was one of the best known business men of America of the day.

label: text
text: During the war he did valuable work in the cause of the Allies with regard to the maintenance of oil supplies.

label: paragraph_title
text: CHEUNG CHAU NOTES

label: text
text: (From Our Own Correspondent.)

label: text
text: No. 2 cottage has changed hands, having been sold to a former old resident, who is making improvements to the property, in the shape of additional servants quarters and a verandah.

label: text
text: This transaction is the 34th or 95th sale that has taken place since the settlement was started, making about 70 different owners. Some of these held their property only for a short period. Ten of the original 80 houses are still held by their builders.

label: text
text: The work at the Police Station seems to have taken a fresh start and the wall work soon finished. The matched which was to have been erected near No. 20 was not put up owing to some new regulation by the P.W.D., all the houses are full and there is still a demand.

label: text
text: The 17th of this month seems to have been a popular day for birthdays, five of the residents (perhaps more) celebrated, and birthday parties were the order; in the evening. A few hours later Mr. Stork gave a surprise party in No. 6, in the early hours of the morning a new Ray came to brighten the household; the little lady and her mother are getting on nicely, later on we had the news that a young gentleman had put in an appearance in the family of one of the Alliance Missionaries, making the third recent addition to that Mission congratulations to all.

label: text
text: Welcome showers have just fallen, to freshen up the gardens which were getting very dry.

label: paragraph_title
text: SEVEN YEARS

label: paragraph_title
text: HEAVY SENTENCE ON PAWN-SHOP ROBBERS.

label: text
text: An important factor in the evidence against three prisoners charged at the Criminal Sessions yesterday afternoon with taking part in a pawnshop robbery was that they had offered some of the stolen jewellery in exchange for opium. Other missing articles were found in the house raided by Inspector F. W. Shaftain and Chinese constables and it was here that the prisoners were found. The total value of the jewellery taken from the pawnshop was $4,900.

label: text
text: The prisoners were identified by witnesses at the Sessions yesterday who were in the pawnshop when the robbers made their entry and who had been put into a small room, gagged and bound.

label: text
text: At the resumed sitting this morning two of the prisoners were found guilty by the jury and sentenced to seven years' imprisonment, whilst the third was discharged as a result of an alibi.
